title: The Drowned Garden
premise: Tamsin Thornbury flees her hedge-witch mistress with nothing but a stolen ledger and a knack for reading the true names of impossible things. The Guild of the Gilded Root, which traffics in bottled storms, borrowed years, and one dying dragon's last fire, hires her to keep its books — unaware she carries the gift the crown has declared punishable by drowning. When the royal hunt reaches the city, Tamsin discovers the ledgers hide a terrible truth: the king died years ago, and a crown-bound entity rules through his borrowed face, sustained by the dragon-fire the Guild secretly sells it. To end the hunt and save the gifted from the drownings, Tamsin must ally with a disgraced huntsman, her vengeful former mistress, and the Guild's ruthless mistress-of-coin to unbind the king's name at the winter solstice — even though doing so will burn out the last dragon-fire and unravel the Guild she has come to love. In the end she chooses truth over the only home she's found, speaks the king's true name, and inherits not a throne but a garden drowned beneath the palace, where the gifted can finally take root in the open.
about_author: Mara Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing merchant ledgers in coastal port towns before turning to fiction. She writes fantasies about bookkeepers, smugglers, and the quiet violence of paperwork.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Fleeing her mistress Odile in a rain-soaked marsh town, Tamsin trades a charm for passage and steals a ledger she believes is worthless. The emotional beat is fear sharpened into defiance; she vows never to be anyone's apprentice again.

chapters.title: A Guild of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the port city of Saltmere, the Guild of the Gilded Root catches her reading the ledger's true names and hires her instead of hanging her. She meets mistress-of-coin Verity Crane and huntsman-castoff Bram Hale. Beat: wary relief — shelter that might be a trap.

chapters.title: The Crown Proclaims a Hunt
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Royal criers announce the gift-hunt; drownings begin in the harbor. Bram, once a royal huntsman, recognizes the decree's seal is wrong — the king's signature has changed. Beat: dread and old guilt resurfacing.

chapters.title: Bottled Storms and Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She learns the Guild's inventory: storms, years, memories, and a single vial of dragon-fire renewed monthly by a mysterious buyer. Her gift lets her read what the ledgers conceal. Beat: fascination curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: What Odile Left in Her
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Odile arrives in Saltmere, publicly disowning Tamsin — a betrayal that shields her from suspicion. Privately Odile warns her: the hunt was written in hedge-magic, and someone at court knows Tamsin's name. Beat: wounded loyalty.

chapters.title: The Drowning of Wren Amsel
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. A gifted Guild courier is taken and drowned by decree; the Guild does nothing. Tamsin watches the crowd cheer and realizes justice outside the law must be built by hand. Beat: grief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Buyer in the Palace
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram infiltrates a court masque and sees the king — and the wrongness wearing him, a shadow that moves a half-second late. He escapes with half a name. Beat: horror and confirmation of his heresy.

chapters.title: Entries in a Dead Man's Hand
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Cross-checking decades of ledgers, Tamsin finds the dragon-fire payments began the month the old king 'recovered' from a fever that should have killed him. Beat: the thrill of the pattern, and its terrible implication.

chapters.title: Verity's Price
chapters.summary: Verity's POV. Verity reveals the Guild's bargain: the crown tolerates the Guild in exchange for the fire that sustains the king. Expose the truth and the Guild burns with the crown. Beat: loyalty versus truth, stated plainly at last.

chapters.title: A Huntsman's Confession
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram admits he once hunted the gifted for the crown, including Tamsin's father. Tamsin must decide whether his remorse is worth trust. Beat: rage, then a fragile, conditional forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Solstice Ledger
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She decodes Odile's hidden marginalia: an unbinding rite requiring the king's true name, spoken at solstice, within the drowned garden beneath the palace. Beat: hope — and the cost, the last dragon-fire, spelled out.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The Guild's deepest vault holds the dragon itself, kept guttering as the Guild's furnace and the crown's life-support. Tamsin meets its eye and it gives her one word of its true name. Beat: awe and moral vertigo.

chapters.title: A Trap Written in Her Own Hand
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A forged requisition lures the Guild's couriers into a crown ambush; Tamsin realizes the hunt's spymaster has been reading her ledgers through a bound clerk. Beat: guilt — her neat handwriting as a weapon against her own people.

chapters.title: Odile's Bargain
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile offers the crown Tamsin's name in exchange for the gifted of her old village — then burns her own half of the contract, choosing her apprentice over her safety. Beat: love expressed as treachery undone.

chapters.title: The Spymaster's Kindness
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Captured briefly by spymaster Corvel, Tamsin is offered freedom, wealth, and legal pardon if she names the gifted. He is genuinely kind, which makes refusing harder than cruelty would. Beat: temptation and clarity.

chapters.title: What the Guild Cannot Forgive
chapters.summary: Verity's POV. Tamsin's escape exposes the Guild; Verity must choose between the ledgers' survival and the people in them. She burns the client lists and sides with Tamsin. Beat: an institution choosing conscience over continuity.

chapters.title: Down Through the Water
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The allies enter the palace cisterns — the drowned garden, an orchard planted by the old king for his gifted daughter. Bram holds the way open against huntsmen. Beat: sacrifice offered, survival uncertain.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the garden, Tamsin confronts the entity: it claims it saved the kingdom from a dying king and a failing land, and that unbinding means famine. Its argument is almost fair. Beat: doubt at the threshold of the climax.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, climax. At solstice, with the dragon-fire spent to fuel the rite, Tamsin speaks the king's true name — the word the dragon gave her. The crown-entity unravels; the true king's bones finally rest. Beat: triumph purchased with the last fire.

chapters.title: Ash and Aftermath
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The hunt collapses without its author; Bram is pardoned and refuses it, choosing the gifted's new council instead. Verity rebuilds the Guild as an open archive. Odile and Tamsin reconcile without pretending the wounds are gone. Beat: weary, honest relief.

chapters.title: The Garden That Learned to Breathe
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The drowned garden drains; where dragon-fire fell, green returns. The gifted come out of hiding to plant it. Tamsin keeps its ledger — of names, not debts. Beat: inheritance redefined as stewardship.

chapters.title: A New Entry, in Her Own Hand
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A year later, Tamsin teaches a runaway apprentice of her own — to read names, to question ledgers, to leave when she must. The final entry she writes is her own true name, freely given. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
